messages.subject: Extract percentile values?
parts:
Hi all;
Suppose that we run a hypothetical simple model and the as you know the estimation output is as follow:

------------------------------------------------
> fit
Inference for Stan model: model.
1 chains, each with iter=10; warmup=5; thin=1; 
post-warmup draws per chain=5, total post-warmup draws=5.

      mean se_mean   sd  2.5%   25%   50%   75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
mu   -0.06    0.08 0.17 -0.27 -0.12 -0.12  0.11  0.12     5 0.76
lp__ -6.85    0.06 0.13 -7.00 -6.96 -6.87 -6.72 -6.72     5 0.76
-----------------------------------------------


How to extract the percentile value (for example 0.12) and save it to a vector for further work on it. 
Note that I want to replicate the model and save the values to a vector.

Best Regards
Mahdi

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Extract percentile values?
parts:
Hi Mahdi, do you mean how do you get quantiles other than the defaults of 2.5%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 97.5%? If you're using RStan and you want the 12% quantile for each parameter then you can do 

fit_summary <- summary(fit, probs = c(0.12))
fit_summary$summary[, "12%"]

The object fit_summary will be a list with two components, c_summary and summary, the former giving you the summary for each chain, and the latter with all chains combined.

Hope that helps, 

Jonah

Ben and Johan, I sincerely thank you for your answers.
Also I get the goal by apply function:
#
apply(fit, MARGIN = "parameters", FUN = quantile, probs = (1:1000) / 1000)
